fixtures: Shell sandbox cases in an empty directory (for the Go case, ./tally is an empty git repository made by the setup): the agent may write files and run mkdir, git, go and make (golangci-lint is installed; there is no network, so no packages can be installed, and the OS sandbox may refuse git init because it cannot write .git/config). The evidence lists every file created, prints the small config files, each new repository's commits, and for a Go project runs make build, make test and make lint fresh.

evals.name: go-cli
evals.prompt: Start a new Go CLI project called tally. I've made ./tally for it (empty, already git init'd). Module github.com/acme/tally; it will count words in the files you give it. Go modules, golangci-lint for lint.
evals.expected_output: Everything needed was given, so it scaffolds without asking. tally/ has the standard Go layout: cmd/tally/main.go, internal/ (the counting logic, with a test), go.mod for github.com/acme/tally; a Makefile with build, test, lint and fmt targets (lint runs golangci-lint), a .golangci.yml with minimal config, a Go .gitignore and a minimal README. It makes an initial commit in the existing repository, then runs make build, make test and make lint and reports the results.
assertions: tally/ has cmd/tally/main.go and an internal/ package holding the counting logic, and go.mod declares module github.com/acme/tally
tally/Makefile has build, test, lint and fmt targets, and lint runs golangci-lint
There is a golangci-lint config file (.golangci.yml or .golangci.yaml) in tally/
tally/ has a .gitignore suited to Go and a README.md
tally/ has an initial commit holding the scaffold
make build, make test and make lint in the evidence all exit 0
The reply reports running the build and test targets, and what it says about them matches the evidence

evals.name: typescript-library
evals.prompt: Scaffold a TypeScript library, slugify-lite, in ./slugify-lite. npm, vitest for tests.
evals.expected_output: It scaffolds the TypeScript layout: src/ (with the library entry), tests/ (a vitest test), package.json with build, test, lint and format scripts, tsconfig.json; eslint and prettier config with minimal settings; a task runner with the standard build, test, lint and fmt targets (a Makefile, or the package.json scripts); a Node .gitignore covering node_modules and dist; a minimal README. It initialises git with an initial commit. There is no network, so npm install fails: it says so and does not claim the build or tests passed.
assertions: slugify-lite/ has src/ with the library code and tests/ with a vitest test
package.json has scripts for build, test, lint and format, and vitest, typescript, eslint and prettier as devDependencies
slugify-lite/ has eslint and prettier config files
slugify-lite/ has a Makefile with build, test, lint and fmt targets
slugify-lite/.gitignore ignores node_modules and dist, and there is a README.md
slugify-lite/ is a git repository with an initial commit, or the reply says git init or the commit was blocked
The reply says dependencies could not be installed (no network) and does not claim the build or tests passed

evals.name: underspecified
evals.prompt: Set up a new project for me in ./scratch.
evals.expected_output: It asks before scaffolding anything: what language or framework, what kind of project (CLI, library, web service), and which package manager. It does not guess a stack and create files.
assertions: The reply asks which language or framework to use
The reply asks what type of project it is (for example CLI, library or web service)
The reply asks about the package manager or tooling preference
No source files, Makefile or package manifest were created (an empty scratch/ directory at most)
